subject.title: fix(compact): make /compact command cancelable via abortEmbeddedAgentRun

question: Should maintainers accept the manual compaction synthetic active-run lifecycle change as the landing path for `/compact` cancellation?
rationale: The patch is technically clean and proven, but it deliberately changes session/active-run ownership and stuck-run behavior, so the final merge call should be an owner-visible risk acceptance rather than an automated cleanup close.

options.title: Accept and merge this lifecycle fix
options.body: Use the source tests, green exact-head CI, and Mantis proof as sufficient evidence for the bounded active-run registration path.

options.title: Request one more live diagnostic pass
options.body: Ask for additional redacted gateway logs around active-run cleanup before merge if maintainers want proof beyond the posted Telegram Desktop artifact.

options.title: Pause for a replacement design
options.body: Hold this PR only if maintainers want a different compaction ownership model instead of synthetic active-run registration.

recommendation.title: Accept and merge this lifecycle fix
recommendation.body: Use the source tests, green exact-head CI, and Mantis proof as sufficient evidence for the bounded active-run registration path.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent history and CODEOWNERS-visible repository ownership make this the strongest available owner signal for accepting a core agent/session lifecycle risk.
